Messages.Author: Hardy Range
Messages.Body:
This happened during our first game with SW:

A player had out Moncada, the Lasombra Cardinal who, amongst other special
abilities, has the following drawback: "Moncada cannot block."
Our Esteemed Cardinal and Plenipotentiary then tried to play an Eternal
Vigilance:

Card Text

Eternal Vigilance
Action, costs 1 blood
Requires a ready Archbishop, Priscus or Cardinal. +1 stealth.
Put this card on the acting vampire. During an action, the Sabbat vampire
with this card can pay a blood to untap and attempt to block. Burn this card
if this Sabbat vampire goes to torpor.

The question is, does the explicit text on EV ("can pay a blood to untap and
attempt to block") override the inability of Moncada to block?
We ruled during the game that the answer is no, but I wanted to be sure. The
answer would be applicable to all other effects that could possibly allow
Moncada to block, I guess.

Another interesting question concerns the wording on EV:
It talks about "this Sabbat vampire" twice. This seems to imply that if the
vampire with the card loses membership in the Sabbat, he cannot use its
effects until he becomes a Sabbat member again. Is that right?
And, more interesting: If the vampire is not Sabbat by the time he goes to
torpor, is EV burned? :-)

--

Sorry, Tim - I did not own the card myself until about two hours ago, so I
hadn't the text here. (BTW, I do agree with people who are upset that there
is talk in this newsgroup about new cards but who are _not_ told what the
card does. But as you may have guessed, I am on the other hand not a very
great fan of posting card text from memory and starting wild rumors...)

So here we go:

Ambrosio Luis Moncada, Plenipotentiary
Lasombra, cap 10, aus for DOM OBT POT PRE
<insert picture of fat, ugly, pale-skinned, bald-headed vampire here>
Sabbat Cardinal
Moncada cannot block. Actions directed at Moncada cost an additional pool.
If Moncada is ready during your discard phase, he can untap another ready
Lasombra.

I think that the card reflects the (late) Sabbat Cardinal from the Clan
Novel series quite well: Moncada never leaves his haven in Madrid (?), so he
cannot block, but is very hard to hit (the Assamite Fatimah was faced with
exactly this problem in one of the novels) - but he has a great lot of
political clout both within his own clan and the Sabbat as a whole.
A minor discrepancy between the WoD as shown in the novels and the reality
:-) of our V:tES is that Moncada is Lucita's Sire, but in the card game the
capacities differ by 2.

Messages.Author: John Whelan
Messages.Body:
On 1 Nov 2000, Halcyan 2 wrote:



Still, I don't think it is necessarily a discrepancy. I do not think that
capacity reflects generation only. It can also indicate other aspects of
power and influence, like the posession of a significant title.
Ordinarily, the equivalencies should be as follows:

Generation Capacity
14 or 15 1
13 2
12 3
11 4
10 5
9 6
8 7
7 8
6 9

This implies that 10 capacity is equivalent to 5th generation, and 11
capacity to 4th. But that is a bit of a problem, because 5th and 4th
generations are Methuselahs, and that's who *we* are supposed to
be. Also, by adding skill cards to vampires, one can easily create
vampires of "First Generation" or lower.

I think it is more reasonable to conclude that no vampires in play are
lower than 6th generation, and capacities higher than 9 represtent factors
other than age (such as resources derived from position). There is plenty
of evidence for this. For instance, certain Praxis Siezures give the
vampire who earns it an extra point of capacity, which he later loses when
he loses the title. Presumably the same might apply to vampires who have
titles naturally. Similarly, when a Justicar loses his title from "Wrath
of the Inner Circle", he loses a point of capacity, implying, perhaps,
that his Justicar status was part of the reason he had a capacity that
high in the first place.

My take on it therefore, would be that Moncada is a 6th generation vampire
who is gains a point of capacity because of his political position.
Lucita, his childe, is 7th generation, but has no political position.

-- John Whelan

I have to admit that you provide an EXCELLENT argument for this and I'm sure
that it is indeed for many cases (especially those "inferior" Sabbat vamps).

Interestingly enough, there ARE a few vamps who seem to fit the original model.

I've always found it amusing that you could influence Etrius, who is himself a
4th generation Methusaleh. And since he is 11 capacity... (maybe there's an
alternative explanation. You're just enlisting his help or enlisting a
simulacrum of him or something). Similarly, I think Ayelea is supposed to be
one of Goratrix's own children so she is appropriately a 10 cap. I should
review Children of the Night again but I *think* Queen Anne's gen also reflects
this. I think Kemintiri is also right.

But then again, this original theory (generation translates directly to
capacity) doesn't always work. I *think* Dylan (!Ventrue) should be a higher
cap. He's only a 6 cap (9th gen) and still manages to make the Most Wanted
List? And I think Al-Ashrad should be a gen higher? I'm no expert on Assamites
but I thought Al-Ashrad was sired by Ur-Shulgi who was sired by Haqim himself.
So...?

But overall I think you have a great theory.

Halcyan 2
